item.title: JU student goes missing; ‘suicide note’ found in hall room
item.description:
Md Mohaiminul Islam, a student of the 50th batch of the Department of Geological Sciences at Jahangirnagar University (JU), has gone missing.
Mohaiminul, from Hazra Bari in Melandah upazila of Jamalpur, was last seen boarding a bus in front of his dormitory at 3:08pm on Sunday, according to university administration sources.
He is a resident student of Room 110 in Block A of the hall. Despite attempts to contact him, his whereabouts remain unknown.
A general diary was filed at Savar police station, and Dhaka District Superintendent of Police Shamima Parvin was informed of the incident.
In a separate notice, the university’s Public Relations Office said a “suicide note” had been found in the student’s room. As the note reportedly mentions negligence by the department, the JU administration has formed an investigation committee.
Professor Dr Muhammad Nazrul Islam, the university’s pro-vice-chancellor (administration), said the university administration, proctorial body and police were working to locate the student. They were also contacting his friends, relatives and acquaintances.
The university authorities have urged anyone with information about Mohaiminul’s whereabouts to contact the proctor at 01714012315 or the security officer at 01712674557.

item.title: Litton ton powers Bangladesh to set Afghanistan 479-run target
item.description:
Bangladesh wicketkeeper-batter Litton Das struck a superb century as the Tigers built a massive target for Afghanistan in the one-off Test at Sheikh Zayed Stadium in Abu Dhabi on Monday.
Litton's hundred strengthened Bangladesh's position in the match after the visitors established a 106-run first-innings lead, thanks largely to a devastating bowling display from Hasan Mahmud and Ebadot Hossain on the third day.
Bangladesh had finished Sunday's play at 223-6 in their second innings, extending their overall lead to 329 runs. Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto scored 82 and veteran batter Mushfiqur Rahim made 81 to rescue the innings after the Tigers slipped to 53-3.
Litton, who resumed the fourth morning unbeaten on five, capitalised on two dropped catches to reach his century and put Bangladesh firmly in control. His partnership with Mehidy Hasan Miraz proved crucial in frustrating Afghanistan's bowlers and extending the visitors' advantage.
Mehidy also made a valuable contribution, supporting Litton as Bangladesh's seventh-wicket stand carried the total beyond 300. The pair's resistance ensured Afghanistan faced a daunting challenge in the fourth innings.
Earlier, Afghanistan were dismissed for 240 in reply to Bangladesh's first-innings 346. Hasan Mahmud claimed 5-55, including a hat-trick, becoming the first Bangladesh fast bowler to achieve the feat in Test cricket. Ebadot Hossain complemented him with four wickets.
Afghanistan captain Rahmat Shah had earlier scored an unbeaten 105, while Abdul Malik contributed 62, but their efforts could not prevent Bangladesh from securing a significant first-innings deficit.
Bangladesh eventually declared their second innings at 372-7, setting Afghanistan a target of 479 runs for victory.
The Tigers will now look to their bowlers to finish the job and secure a memorable Test victory.

item.title: 'Amazing feeling': Hasan reflects on historic Test hat-trick
item.description:
Bangladesh quick Hasan Mahmud has admitted it was a surreal feeling when he became the first fast bowler from his country to complete a Test hat-trick.
Mahmud completed the feat in the one-off Test against Afghanistan in Abu Dhabi when he ripped through the opposition's batting lineup on his way to collecting another five-wicket haul.
The right-armer becomes just the third player from Bangladesh to register a hat-trick in a Test match and the first fast bowler to do so, joining Alok Kapali (v Pakistan in 2003) and Sohag Gazi (v New Zealand in 2013) as the only players from the country to register three consecutive dismissals in a Test.
Mahmud first deceived Ismat Alam to uproot his off-stump, before he removed Qais Ahmad and Zia-ur-Rehman with consecutive deliveries to clinch the rare hat-trick.
“It's an amazing feeling," Mahmud said at stumps on day three of the Test after Bangladesh reached 223/6 in their second innings to lead by 329 runs overall.
"When you start bowling and see movement off the wicket, you try to bowl upright, swing the ball and get a wicket.
"I was just trying that and following my process. I was pleased to see this kind of movement in the morning."
It helped continue a rich vein of form for Mahmud, who in August led Bangladesh to a memorable Test triumph over Australia in Darwin with a nine-wicket match haul as the side continued their push up the ICC World Test Championship standings.
This fixture against Afghanistan isn't part of the World Test Championship cycle, but Mahmud's form was just as impressive as the seamer collected four wickets overall on the third day to finish with figures of 5/55 from 21 economical overs.
Mahmud paid credit to Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto and experienced batter Litton Das for playing their part in the hat-trick, after the duo convinced him to review the decisive LBW decision against Zia-ur-Rehman to ensure he completed the feat.
“Last day I only got one wicket the whole day, but I wasn't nervous at all. I was looking forward to today,” Mahmud said.
“We lost a couple of DRS in the first innings, so everyone was thinking about the DRS, whether it was going to be hitting or not. Credit to the captain and Litton Das. They were talking and chatting with each other, and then they told me that it was going to hit, so I could take the review.
“I just felt that I should bowl straight. That's it. Let the ball do the job. So I just followed the line and bowled at the top of the stumps."

item.title: Isco nets brace as Betis rise back above Real Madrid to third
item.description:
Veteran playmaker Isco struck twice to help Real Betis climb back into third place in La Liga with a 5-2 win over Osasuna on Sunday.
The Andalucian side moved a point above Real Madrid, fourth, and level with second place Atletico Madrid, trailing leaders Barca by five points.
Manuel Pellegrini's side claimed a sixth league win from eight matches with an exciting display of attacking football at La Cartuja stadium, where they are playing until their Benito Villamarin home is renovated, likely 2028.
Former Real Madrid midfielder Isco, 34, netted from the penalty spot after a foul on Rodrigo Riquelme, and Ez Abde doubled the hosts lead after half-an-hour with a cool finish.
Ante Budimir's own goal gave Betis their third after half-time, before the Croatian striker netted at the correct and Raul Garcia added another to give Osasuna a fighting chance.
Isco capitalised on a loose ball in the box to grab his second and Jose Morante bagged a fifth in stoppage time to close out Betis's big win.
"Football is never truly under control," said Pellegrini after his side almost let their three-goal lead slip.
"As soon as the pace drops, the other team can pull level."
The former Manchester City coach also praised Isco after his brace.
"He has spectacular quality and a maturity as a player that allows him to perform at whatever level he wants to," added Pellegrini.
Elsewhere Valencia, 19th, earned a point in a 2-2 draw at Racing Santander under new coach Javier Aguirre.
Real Sociedad defeated Deportivo La Coruna 3-2 in another entertaining battle.
The Basque side, sixth, eased into a three-goal lead Mario Soriano pulled one back for the visitors in San Sebastian to spark a Depor fight back.
They were given further encouragement when Real Sociedad's Pablo Marin was sent off in the 66th minute for a foul on Nsongo Bil in the box and Yeremay Hernandez netted from the penalty spot.
Both teams finished with 10 men after Lorenzo Amatucci brought down Mikel Oyarzabal as the last man, and Depor could not find an equaliser.
On Saturday Liga leaders Barcelona beat Getafe 3-0 to prolong their perfect start to the season, with eight wins from eight league games.
Hansi Flick's side are followed by second place Atletico Madrid, who snatched a late 2-1 win at Alaves, while Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid scraped a 1-0 victory over Villarreal despite Vinicius Junior's red card for hair-pulling.

item.title: City shrug off uncertain future to beat 10-man Liverpool
item.description:
Manchester City shrugged off the threat of swingeing sanctions to beat 10-man Liverpool 3-0 in their first game since being found guilty on more than 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules.
Second-half goals from Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki extended City's flawless start under Enzo Maresca after Ryan Gravenberch had been sent off for two yellow cards.
City re-established their three-point lead at the top of the table, but the future of any title challenge rests on the outcome of the club's appeal against widespread financial impropriety.
"We need to learn how to deal with the outside noise, but make our own noise, which is to win games," said Maresca.
"Our fans were singing at the end, so the noise was from us."
An independent commission found City and their Emirati owners arranged "sham" deals to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion) between 2009 and 2018.
No sanction has yet been handed down, but a severe points deduction or even expulsion from the English top flight are on the table unless City overturn the decision.
There has even been speculation there could be retrospective action to strip titles.
"The uncertainty is not good for anyone," said Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola.
The multiple breaches of Premier League laws came during a period in which City won three titles and a clutch of other trophies.
City's rivals believe, however, that the illegal spending during that period also built the foundations for a golden era under former boss Pep Guardiola, who left at the end of last season.
Liverpool were one of the clubs most affected, having finished second to City three times in the past 12 years.
"City have fundamentally cheated to win those leagues," Jamie Gallaghie, a 48-year-old teacher, told AFP.
The visitors arrived under the protection of a police escort with a hostile Anfield welcome expected, but there was no repeat of the violent scenes when their team bus was pelted by bottles ahead of a Champions League clash in 2018.
Liverpool fans lined the streets to greet the City players with chants of "cheats" and "going down", while merchandise stalls were littered with flags and scarves mocking their rivals' financial scandal.
In the iconic Kop end behind one goal a banner read "a generation of supporters cheated."
The battles between Guardiola's City and Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool in recent years became the Premier League's marquee event.
But with the eyes of the world watching, Liverpool failed to rise to the occasion on the field.
New Liverpool boss Iraola's options were blunted without the injured Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo as the Spaniard suffered his first defeat since taking charge of the Reds.
An Abu Dhabi-backed takeover in 2008 transformed City from mid-table mediocrity into the dominant force of the English game.
City's economic might was on full show and helped turn the game as Maresca could introduce Doku off the bench early in the second half.
Within minutes the Belgian winger had been chopped down by Gravenberch, who was shown a harsh second booking, and Liverpool never recovered.
Doku's deflected shot was then smashed home by Haaland to break the deadlock 25 minutes from time, opening the floodgates.
Three minutes later Doku curled a sensational strike into the top corner himself.
Cherki then exchanged a slick one-two with Josko Gvardiol before slotting under Alisson Becker to rub salt in Liverpool wounds.
The defeat leaves Liverpool nine points adrift of the leaders down in ninth.

item.title: Abhishek, Arshdeep shine in India's Indore triumph
item.description:
A run-filled contest took over in Indore as a collective 432 runs were scored across 40 overs, with India ultimately emerging victors by 14 runs and going ahead 2-1 in the five-match T20I series.
Opener Abhishek Sharma top-scored for India with a quickfire 69 as the hosts amassed a good total of 223 and a disciplined bowling performance ensured the West Indies were held to just 209/7 in reply.
Left-armer Arshdeep Singh (3/44) was the pick of the bowlers and was adjudged Player of the Match for his efforts, but India skipper Shreyas Iyer was impressed with the performance from his entire bowling group.
"It was wonderful to see the bowlers being confident," Iyer said post-match.
"The clarity was very much visible when I was interacting. They were ready to take up the challenge and that's what we want."
West Indies captain Shai Hope was left to lament a couple of telling mistakes with the ball that allowed India to post such a competitive total.
"Probably with the ball, we could've executed a little bit better," Hope said.
"So those little margins would be the deciding factor come the end of the game."
India were put in to bat first and after Sanju Samson fell for just three runs, Abhishek took charge of the innings with a blistering 69 off 30 deliveries, which included six fours and five sixes.
Ishan Kishan continued the assault, scoring a quickfire 37 off 18 balls as India raced to 115 in just 8.2 overs. Roston Chase brought Kishan's innings to an end to provide the West Indies with a timely breakthrough.
Tilak Varma added further impetus with a brisk 28 off 16 deliveries before a bizarre run-out cut short his stay at the crease.
India maintained their aggressive approach in the latter stages, with Nitish Kumar Reddy (21 off 14) and Axar Patel (20 off 14) chipping in with valuable contributions to keep the scoreboard moving.
Prince Yadav then provided a late flourish, striking three boundaries in the final over as India were bowled out for 223.
Chase (2/38), Shamar Springer (2/54) and Shamar Joseph (2/54) claimed two wickets apiece for the visitors.
In reply, the West Indies endured a disastrous start as Hope, who had struck a century in the second T20I, was cleaned up by Arshdeep for five in the second over.
Shimron Hetmyer and Kamil Pooran then launched a spirited counterattack, putting together a 60-run partnership for the second wicket off just 31 deliveries.
Hetmyer smashed 43 off 26 balls, while Pooran contributed 42 off 27, briefly shifting the momentum in the visitors' favour.
Naman Dhir, however, struck at a crucial juncture to dismiss both set batters and swing the contest back in India's favour.
Sherfane Rutherford (32 off 20) and Quentin Sampson (21 off 15) attempted to revive the chase, but India continued to chip away at the wickets and prevented the West Indies from building another substantial partnership.
Springer brought out some surprise fireworks at the end with a breathtaking 35* from just 11 balls, but India ultimately sealed the deal by 14 runs.
Arshdeep led the bowling effort with figures of 3/44, receiving valuable support from Naman Dhir (2/39), Axar Patel (1/33) and Nitish Kumar Reddy (1-19).
The fourth T20I will take place in Hyderabad on Wednesday, 14 October.

item.title: Sadaqat, Imran help Pakistan thump Sri Lanka to seal T20 series
item.description:
Maaz Sadaqat just missed out on a hundred as Pakistan upstaged Sri Lanka by 82 runs in the second T20 international on Sunday, taking an unbeatable 2-0 lead in the series.
Sadaqat's 51-ball 96 and Sahibzada Farhan's 44-ball 73 helped Pakistan to their highest T20 total at home of 215-3 in Rawalpindi.
Medium pacer Mohammad Imran then grabbed 3-11 to restrict Sri Lanka to 133-7 for Pakistan's biggest T20 win over the tourists.
Sri Lanka lost wickets at regular intervals with Maheesh Theekshana (32 not out) and Chamindu Wickramasinghe (29) offering some resistance once the game was beyond reach.
Kamindu Mendis (23) and Sineth Jayawardena (22) were the only others to reach double figures.
Pakistan benefited from three dropped catches by Sri Lanka as Sadaqat and Farhan punished the attack, adding 88 runs for the second wicket off just 49 balls.
Sadaqat smashed seven sixes -- the joint most by a Pakistan batter in a T20s -- and six fours before being dismissed off the final delivery of the innings.
Farhan, dropped on two and 11, hit five sixes and four fours before he holed out to Dasun Shanaka in the 15th over.
Sadaqat, who was put down on 44, then cut loose and added a quickfire 72 off 31 balls for the third wicket with Hasan Nawaz (19 not out).
Pakistan plundered 70 runs in the last five overs, improving on their highest home T20 total of 208-3 against the West Indies in Karachi five years ago.
The third and final match is on Tuesday.

item.title: France’s high school students plan fresh protests
item.description:
France’s high school students on Monday begin a new stage of their campaign for improved conditions, hoping to maintain the momentum with a fresh wave of demonstrations.
The new protests, scheduled for Tuesday, could be a turning point in the movement, launched in mid-September, which the government hopes is already winding down.
On Friday, the government noted a dramatic drop in the number of blockades and meetings outside the country’s lycees, where students -- most between 15 and 18 -- complete their high school education.
More than 96% were opening Friday, said the education ministry.
The authorities are all the more keen to see the student protests end given that online activists have called for demonstrations next Saturday to protest the cost of living.
For President Emmanuel Macron’s administration, that brings back troubling memories of the grassroots Yellow Vest movement.
Their protests, launched in 2018 over a planned fuel tax rise, saw massive demonstrations and clashes between police and protesters that shook the presidency during Macron’s first term in office.
The government is still counting the cost of the high school protests.
A government source told journalists last week that the cost for damage caused by the demonstrations was “at least 30 million euros.”
On Friday, the justice ministry said more than 6,800 people had been detained since the demonstrations started, 86 percent of them minors.
After clashes between some protesters and riot police left some students severely injured, sparking criticism of police tactics, the government suspended the use of stun grenades that cost one student his hand.
Police are investigating 18 alleged cases of misconduct within their ranks.
Last week, the government came up with concrete proposals to try to address the students’ demands.
Education Minister Edouard Geffray announced late Thursday that some 3,000 substitute teachers would be deployed in the coming days to replace absent staff at the 114 worst-affected high schools.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu on Sunday promised to make changes to the planned budget 2027 to respond to some demands set out in an online platform the government set up to gather students’ views.
The student organizations behind the protests are yet to be convinced, however.
The Union of High School students described the initial announcements last week as “crumbs.” They are maintaining their demand for an extra 10 million euros to be invested in the country’s lycees.
France’s 10,000 medical students, however, are beginning to express concern at the effect any continued school blockades could have on exams starting Monday that help determine their eventual speciality.
They do not want to see the students’ action disrupt such a crucial stage of their education.
Last Thursday’s student demonstrations mobilized tens of thousands of people across France: 71,500 according to interior ministry figures.
Nearly 256,000 took part in last Tuesday’s day of action.
And one poll, carried out by Ipsos-BVA and published on Sunday, said 54% of respondents backed the high school student protests.
They had the most sympathy with student complaints about the excessive size of classes and with the need to renovate the country’s crumbling schools.
